clue.text: Without a rival, but still unmarried

definitions.meaning: having no equal or peer anywhere
without a marriage match

explanation.definitionFit: Peerless and unequalled mean the same; read literally, someone with no match has not yet been wed.

clue.text: Ain't disposed to be one of the opposition

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to join the opposition party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges the four letters of AINT; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A person against something is described by the prefix-turned-noun meaning an opponent.

clue.text: Believes additions to the account

definitions.meaning: trusts or accepts as true
sums entered on the plus side of a bank or ledger account

explanation.definitionFit: To give credence is to believe; in bookkeeping, sums paid in are entries on the plus side of a ledger.

clue.text: C ave spotter

definitions.meaning: the Latin schoolboy warning cry, 'beware!', shouted when a teacher approaches
a person posted to watch for danger

explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'Cave' in two. 'Cave' is not a hole in a hill: it is the Latin warning (KAY-vee) British schoolboys once called out when a master approached.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin warning cry translates as 'beware', a shouted warning; a sentry posted to watch is also called by the same two words run together.

clue.text: All the points of a needle have been used

definitions.text: All the points of a needle have been used

parts.words: All the points of a needle have been used
parts.note: a compass needle has four cardinal points, south, east, west and north; their initials together give a word for stitched, i.e. a sewing needle has been used

explanation.surface: Every sharp tip of a sewing needle is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The needle is a compass needle as well as a sewing one: the initials of its four cardinal points spell a word for stitched.
explanation.definitionFit: When a sewing needle has been put to work, the cloth has been stitched.

clue.text: Doctor of philosophy encountered doctor medicine

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Doctor of philosophy encountered doctor medicine' gives MET + PHYSICIAN or PHYSIC but has no source for the A in METAPHYSICIAN; words appear lost (perhaps 'a doctor of medicine')
annotationWithheld.clue: Doctor of philosophy encountered doctor medicine

clue.text: Reminded Peter the outcome is inevitable

indicators.note: the outcome of shuffling is a new arrangement of the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone tells Peter that the result cannot be avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outcome' signals the anagram of REMINDED and PETER, thirteen letters; 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something settled in advance, decided beforehand, cannot be avoided.

clue.text: Pot-bellied footballer?

parts.note: a player with a big belly has his middle sticking out ahead of him, a humorous take on the attacking position at the centre of the front line

explanation.surface: A soccer player has a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunchy player's middle sticks out ahead of him, punning on the striker who plays in the middle of the attack.

clue.text: Gun accident resulting from earlier shot

definitions.meaning: a dangerous blowback of flame from a firearm's breech
a scene in a film showing events from the past

explanation.definitionFit: A firearm can blow flame backwards dangerously; a film scene cutting back in time to show past events has the same name.

clue.text: Their presence isn't otherwise less polite inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece sits within the shuffled letters
otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of isn't are rearranged

explanation.surface: Their presence isn't anything other than rather rude, indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: these are the people whose presence is unwelcome, and the surface's 'isn't otherwise' hides the shuffle signal 'otherwise' acting on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespassers are people who barge in uninvited, so it is their being there that is the problem.

clue.text: Be inclined to slim

definitions.meaning: slope or tilt, or tend towards
thin, having little fat

explanation.definitionFit: To slope or tend is one sense; thin and spare, without fat, is the other.

clue.text: American soldier obtained a leg of mutton

parts.note: GI is the standard term for a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US serviceman managed to get hold of a joint of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: GIGOT is the French and culinary word for a leg of lamb or mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary name for a roasting joint from the sheep's hind limb.

clue.text: Arabian city in which thieves congregate?

definitions.meaning: a port city in Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula
a lair or hideout, as in the phrase 'a den of thieves', with the article included

explanation.definitionFit: The Yemeni seaport is one sense; split into two words it is a lair, the proverbial hideout of thieves.

clue.text: Additional payment if getting on bus going around

indicators.note: the bus goes around the other piece, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Extra pay for anyone who boards a bus as it travels its route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if getting' is linking; the surface's passenger boarding a bus hides a simple container.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra sum paid on top of normal wages, a reward or premium.

clue.text: Minister of a king following Victoria

indicators.note: following places the article and the king after the short name

parts.note: Vic is the short form of the name Victoria
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A church minister belonging to a monarch who came after Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: R is from Latin rex, king, as in royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is a minister of religion.

clue.text: They comprise several classes of fish

definitions.meaning: places of education divided into many forms or classes
shoals: large groups of fish swimming together

explanation.definitionFit: Educational establishments are made up of many classes; large groups of fish swimming together are also so called.

clue.text: Spinner of yarns who tries to spin you a yarn?

definitions.meaning: a worker or machine that twists threads together

definitions.text: who tries to spin you a yarn?
definitions.meaning: a swindler or cheat who tells lies

explanation.definitionFit: One who twists strands into thread; also a dishonest person who cheats you with a tall story.

clue.text: Unglazed porcelain on the tea-table

definitions.meaning: pottery fired once but not yet glazed
a cookie served with tea

explanation.definitionFit: Pottery fired but unglazed is one sense; the sweet baked snack set out at teatime is the other.

clue.text: Teased young Edward about his uncle's wife

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the short name goes round the relative

parts.note: Ted is a familiar short name for Edward
an uncle's wife is an aunt

explanation.surface: Little Ted mocked his aunt by marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a family quarrel; the uncle's wife is simply the relative by marriage, enclosed by the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocked and provoked with jeering remarks.

clue.text: Burnt out through having worked as a domestic

definitions.meaning: blackened and scorched by fire
a char is a cleaning woman, so this is the past tense of doing that job

explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaner who does housework for pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorched black by fire; also the past tense of 'char', to work as a cleaning woman.

clue.text: Business worry

definitions.meaning: a firm or company
anxiety or care

explanation.definitionFit: A firm or commercial enterprise; also anxiety or care.

clue.text: Pile of hay in the fowlyard

definitions.meaning: a small conical heap of hay in a field
the male bird found among poultry

explanation.definitionFit: A haystack heap in a field shares its name with the male chicken in a farmyard.

clue.text: Navy goes in but exposed to fire

indicators.note: goes in means the navy is placed within the other word

explanation.surface: The fleet joins in, but is now under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is the usual crossword source of these two letters; 'but' is taken literally, not as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been put in fire and so scorched.

clue.text: A pastry recipe for mole

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A pastry recipe for a Mexican sauce or a burrowing creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' is not the animal but a harbour breakwater; R for recipe comes from Latin, the Rx symbol on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone breakwater or jetty projecting into the sea.

clue.text: Note from doctor to me

indicators.note: to means the doctor is attached after the other word

explanation.surface: A message a GP sends to me.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is a common crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written message, a memorandum.

clue.text: Does follow stock exchange speculator

definitions.meaning: a male deer goes after the female deer, does
one who buys new shares to sell at once for profit

explanation.definitionFit: The male deer pursues hinds; a speculator who buys new share issues to sell quickly is also named after this animal.

clue.text: Was it for those who couldn't afford a tanner for footwear?

definitions.text: Was it for those who couldn't afford a tanner for footwear?

parts.words: Was it for those who couldn't afford a tanner for footwear?
parts.note: a tanner is both a sixpence and a leather worker; the joke reads the glossy shoe material as hide protected by an invention licence instead of being tanned

explanation.surface: A question about poor people's footwear before they could pay sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is old British slang for a sixpence coin, and also someone who cures hides; the glossy shoe leather is varnished, not tanned.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy varnished hide used for smart shoes, playfully read as skin that never needed tanning.

clue.text: The era of sovereign content

parts.note: a sovereign is a British gold coin, so a period made of its metal; also a period of contented rule, an idealised time of prosperity

explanation.surface: A time when the monarch was happy.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a British gold coin; 'content' is its metal, not happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary period of peace and prosperity, named after the precious yellow metal.
